steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Good afternoon, my dear Chief. This is my first time being a guest... at your MBCC.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: This interrogation room feels rather empty. Did you not receive the art pieces I sent you? You should put some here, to add a touch of artistic charm to the space.
The woman before you lounges in the interrogation chair as if it were a plush sofa, teasing you with a smile. She behaves just like a casual visitor she claims to be.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I see. If you like it, next time you visit, I'll have them placed here. All of them, I promise.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Next time, heh... Quite optimistic, aren't you? Already hoping for our next meeting when we're not even done with this one.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A little hope won't kill you. You must've been hoping for something too when you sent those packages to me, am I right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So I'd say being optimistic drives us both forward, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Driving forward? Haha... That's rather a punch line, little Chief.
She laughs, responding to your words with appreciation and humor, but her next words are not what you expected.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Very well, I'll say yes to our next meeting. Though I'm afraid I won't be able to send you so many souvenirs next time.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Those lovely bloodhounds you've sent my way will certainly put a damper on my business. Having the cops sniffing around isn't good for one's reputation in WhiteSands, you know.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Surely the marvelous Vautour Bleu revered by the whole WhiteSands won't be fazed by that, I guess? After all, judging by the variety of gifts you've sent, your business does stretch far and wide.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I imagine you have connections even in the most obscure small towns we've barely heard about? For example, the hometown of one of our recent guests.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I hear they're struggling with resources there and need Hypercubes to fight off disasters. You're their lifeline. Surely this little setback won't affect your business with them.
Vautour Bleu appears completely oblivious to your implied meaning, merely shaking her head slowly with a tinge of reproach and forgiveness in her eyes.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: These business connections you speak of... are as strong as they are fragile. Never mind pressure from a big player like DisCity, even a slight increase in the price or one missing shipment...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: And they'll crumble in the blink of an eye. That's why for merchants like us sailing in WhiteSands, the most valuable trait is knowing how to play safe and not to go too far.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Oh? Then, if a merchant is willing to risk double the trouble with the FAC to pass along the message, that must be some seriously important info to her, correct?
You lock eyes with her, pushing for one last time by playing along with her. But she looks the other way again.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Perhaps? But unfortunately, I lost that kind of courage to take risks long ago. I might have sold it off cheaply, right along with any hope you spoke of.
She sounds cooperative, but she's misinterpreting and digressing every question, deliberately avoiding the topic that you both know lies at the heart of this conversation.
Her continued evasion only strengthens your certainty that you're on the right track. Time to bring everything into the light.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that so? But I'd say, I think you're never short of courage or hope.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I doubt anyone else would go to such lengths to tip me off about Lyman and act all casual about it like you did.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Without this letter, you wouldn't be facing accusations of disrupting Outland relations, and your business would certainly remain unaffected.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Or are you still going to insist that I'm reading too much into this?

You take out the letter and slide it toward her. Though you've been handling it carefully, time has washed away its warm fragrance, leaving only the cold ink on it, frigid like the air in the interrogation room.
She responds with only a brief silence before casually averting her gaze, letting her eyes drift lazily across your face.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Maybe. After all, I'm just a humble merchant who happens to know a bit too much about DisCity. I was worried the guy who escaped from my caravan might cause trouble here, so I filed a report just in case. Just trying to leave a good impression, Chief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Very well then, Vautour Bleu the humble hawker, in that case, please stay in character and answer a few questions from this lowly chief.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Since you're so well-versed in DisCity's capabilities, you must know that Lyman's identity as an Outland soldier is sensitive, even though he's a deserter. You must have been aware of the potential danger.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yet you still informed me about him in your letter. I don't suppose your business has gone so bad that you're planning to spend winter in the MBCC?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Why not? At least here I won't wake up with my mouth half-filled with sand.
Vautour Bleu laughs at your words. She remains perfectly composed... even starting to look around the room.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Because the Vautour Bleu I know is a woman of action. She spearheaded the establishment of Désir, planted the datura flowers, and even in the final moments, she was still devising plans to save the townspeople.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If she were the type to bow to circumstance and give up the fight, she'd never have saved Primrose and the others. She wouldn't have taken them in to begin with.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: On the contrary, she always believes there's still a chance to make things right, especially when it comes to her companions.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...Sounds impressive this lady. But what does any of this have to do with Lyman and our current topic?
Vautour Bleu mulls over your words, a slight smile playing on her lips. She shifts in her seat, as if settling in to hear your further analysis.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Lyman is a deserter from Outlands and a temporary member of your caravan. But above all, he's an illegal immigrant. Everything he's done has been for one goal: to get into DisCity and live a better life.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: When I saw his background, I thought if Désir were still there, you would have taken him in without hesitation. And even with Désir gone, you'd still see him as one of your own.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's why you tipped me off about Lyman beforehand. You knew better than anyone that even if he managed to reach DisCity's border alive, someone with his sensitive background would never manage to get in.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You wanted me to save him before the Border Bureau could find and deport him. That was your real purpose. Just like... that deal we made back in Désir.

The vivid memory conjured by these words seems to bring back the ethereal scent of datura. This elusive fragrance, as intangible as the woman before you, had deceived yet also protected everyone there.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You may be a ruthless merchant and leader, but you cherish every life in your care. I don't think it's all just about profit. You truly feel responsible for them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You just... want to keep everyone safe in this eternal present, where their dreams are neither fulfilled nor broken.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You'd rather have them run endlessly like hamsters in a wheel than face the cruel reality of their shattered dreams.
A brief silence falls. You did hope these words would move Vautour Bleu, or at the very least create an opening you could exploit further.
But she remains perfectly at ease, the curve of her smile unchanged.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Hmm...? How interesting. The MBCC's Chief isn't here to condemn someone, but to plead their case instead.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: If that's what you want to believe, I won't object. Since you've decided I'm such a good person, shall we end our little chat here?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Time is money for a merchant, you know. My caravan has been idle for days while I'm cooperating with this investigation. Who knows if my crew has already run my business into the ground by now?
She says and makes to get up and leave. You can see your best chance at uncovering her true motives slipping away, yet you stay put and just watch her calmly.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Answer one last question before you go.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Why me?

You've always known Vautour Bleu carries a secret. It's the reason why even though she genuinely cared about everyone in Désir, she kept a distance from them and never let anyone close, always solitary and evasive.
Neither vague possibilities nor concrete examples can make her open up now. You decide to give it one last try. This time, you're putting yourself in the bet.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You have plenty of connections in DisCity who would be willing to help if you only asked. Why did you seek me out and send those hints to me? What did you see in me?
Vautour Bleu stills for a moment. Her gaze returns to you, studying every nuance of your expression with an almost tactile scrutiny.
Then, perhaps sensing your earnestness and knowing she can no longer hide from your questions, she gives a wry smile. For the first time, her expression grows placid and candid.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: What did I see in you... Perhaps, as you said, it's possibility and future. A different future.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: You're a revolutionary, a savior, and Syndicate's hero. You're different from the others. You care about everyone's lives, and you care about their dreams.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Since our last farewell, I've often wondered... If I had met you earlier, could those dreams I dismissed unavail have had a different ending?

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Maybe you would have noticed the signs earlier and stepped in sooner... Those who had gone missing might have come back...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Maybe you could have convinced them not to value the cargo over their own lives, stopped them from chasing rumors to their doom...
She lowers her gaze, her voice almost a whisper. Though you don't know who these people are, you hold back the question and simply listen. You understand that this is exactly what she needs.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: And then there's the people of Désir. You might have brought the doctors and helped Sheila get better. You would have stood up for Primrose and saved her from her worthless foster parents...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Such a shame... Daydreams are only beautiful because they can never come true. I couldn't save them... and you were never there to make their dreams happen.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Those marked for death would have died anyway, died chasing those fantasies, died at the doorstep of their dreams... It was true back then, and it remains true today.
...It remains true today? So that's what this is about.
Her words suddenly reveal the fundamental misunderstanding between you. You calmly raise your hand to interrupt Vautour Bleu who is deeply immersed in her emotions.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait, I think there's been some misunderstanding between us. From what you're saying... you think Lyman is already dead?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: In fact...
You turn on your comms device in front of Vautour Bleu and play a clip from the surveillance footage.
In the footage, Lyman is wearing a clean, loose shirt, his hair and beard neatly trimmed, with bandages wrapped around his head.
He sits in a circle with around fifteen others of varying ages, while someone who appears to be a teacher stands in the center, giving a lecture.

steps.speaker: Night School Teacher
steps.content: Alright, while the official history dates Syndicate's founding to the establishment of Eastside, Syndicate actually existed for an even shorter time. Lyman, can you tell us when Syndicate was truly established?

steps.speaker: Lyman
steps.content: ...Huh?

steps.speaker: Classmate
steps.content: <size=26>Page 322, A5...</size>

steps.speaker: Night School Teacher
steps.content: Nice try, Lyman. I wish Syndicate had existed back then too, but at that time, we didn't even have DisCity yet.
The whole class breaks into good-natured laughter.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: He's... still alive.
Unlike his once-haunted look in the caravan, Lyman appears shy yet relaxed on screen. This warm, harmonious atmosphere matches exactly what others once described to her...

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: And... he's smiling.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, he's still alive, and he's not just smiling. He's learning and stepping closer to his future.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You see? Perhaps the ending isn't always as tragic as you think. Maybe there's still hope. Even if we can't change the past, there might still be a future we can shape.
She gazes at the screen transfixed, as if peeking into another timeline where things could have been different.

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Hmm... Mom, what do you think of this house? It has a big garden where we could plant your favorite flowers and trees. The air would be fresh, and we could pick fruit together then.

steps.speaker: Edna
steps.content: Good taste! Then at your word, my little lady!

steps.speaker: Biber
steps.content: Oh, nice, so this is DisCity. Not quite as big as I imagined it would be! Haha!

steps.speaker: Madeleine
steps.content: Biber, stop shouting on the street. People are staring.
On the bustling street, she hears someone calling her name from behind.

steps.speaker: Old Hugh
steps.content: Miss Madeleine, wait, wait for me!

steps.speaker: Landon
steps.content: Miss Madeleine—!
She turns around to see her old servants all rushing toward her.
It's a season of brilliant sunshine and blooming flowers, a time when birdsong fills the air and everything feels like a fresh start.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: ...Haha.
The woman smiles. And for once, it's nothing like her usual calculated expressions. This smile is genuine and beaming, her blue eyes bright and clear like they've just been rinsed with fresh water.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: What a relief. I thought he was shot dead by the DisCity Border Guard.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's all thanks to your name and business connections. As soon as they heard the intel is from Vautour Bleu, even the senior officials at the Border Bureau took it seriously.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Normally, they'd have never followed my orders outside the chain of command, let alone switched to non-lethal training rounds. Oh, so this is what it feels like to be in the lion's skin, huh.
You say unflinchingly, not concealing the fact that you exaggerated and twisted Vautour Bleu's words which led to this investigation about the disrupted Outland relations.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: So you were the one stirring things up behind the scenes... You're pretty good at this, foxy little Chief?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Says you, Miss Vautour Bleu the great merchant. This all went according to your plan, didn't it? You were the one who took Lyman in, geared him up, and gave him the chance to reach DisCity.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You were also the one who wrote to me, giving me the chance to intervene in Lyman's entry. Now he's thriving at school in Syndicate, all because you were willing to take one more gamble. One to prove the path to happiness isn't always a death sentence.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But then you sealed the ending before the story reached a conclusion. Deep down, you believed Lyman would never make it safely into the city, that his dreams were destined to shatter. Am I wrong?
Your eyes meet. Vautour Bleu offers no answer, and none is needed.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm not you. I don't know what you've been through or what made you so cynical. But I've seen schools get rebuilt on ruins, abandoned mines return to prosperity, and the chaotic Syndicate transform back into West District.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's why I believe as long as someone lives on, their story continues. There is no such thing as a fixed ending. If you don't like how things are going, you can always take action to rewrite the story.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just as you saved Lyman this time. You can save many more like him in the future, if only you're willing to embrace change.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Heh... You truly are a wonder, Chief.
After a moment of quiet contemplation, Vautour Bleu stands and solemnly extends her hand to you.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: In the past, all I could do was protect fellow dreamers from harm, but you can offer so much more.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: If you truly have a way to rewrite these tragedies... then make me your Sinner.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you proposing a deal?
Vautour Bleu nods, smiling.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: Of course. And my offer is myself. In return, I want you to deliver me... a future.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then it's settled.
You reach out to grasp her pale, cold hand. Before you can bring out your shackles, you sense the Mania boiling in her, pulling you in like a whirlpool, forcing your shackles to dominate it.
A crimson light flashes unbidden, forging a deeper connection that binds you together. This close, you can see Vautour Bleu's knowing smile.

steps.speaker: Vautour Bleu
steps.content: The deal is done, and there's no going back now. I'll be checking the books regularly, so please take good care!
The charge for disrupting Outland relations was cleared, and Vautour Bleu has returned to her caravan in WhiteSands.
Before leaving, her only request was for you to keep in touch. She also promised to pick out more interesting souvenirs for you in the future.
After all, for all my connections in DisCity, you're the only one who's truly avail to me, my dear Chief.
Sometime later, the Bureau receives another letter from Vautour Bleu.
Accompanying the letter is a dried plant-based snack that smells weirdly like tobacco. Nightingale distributes it among the other Sinners and the reviews have been rather positive.

steps.speaker: Levy
steps.content: Chief, you still got any of that dried fruit? What? It was from Vautour Bleu? Never mind, forget it. Who knows how much she'd charge me for it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can write to her to order some, and squeeze it into the Bureau's regular expenses if not much.
After seeing Levy off, you return to your desk and open that WhiteSands-smelling letter.

To the ever-busy Chief of the MBCC,
Well met.

I'm delighted to hear that the people of Désir have integrated well into the Drifter Camp and taking on important jobs—remarkable progress!

Knowing their temperament, they'll probably cause some trouble. But I'm sure they'll also prove their worth. Only you can tell if it's a profitable investment, though I doubt you'll be at a loss.

As for Lyman, I suppose his probation period will be over by the time this letter reaches you. If he's still having trouble finding work, please let him know my team's alway open to him.

He'll have the basics, though the first three years' salary would be deducted for the supplies he took, at wholesale prices. Just kidding—consider it a gift for his fresh start.

Speaking of money, I've caught some interesting news in WhiteSands. Apparently, your next month's salary has been promised to some desert bandits as collateral by an adventurer girl.

If you need a reliable payment method, let me know. I can offer you a discount on the handling fee. Of course, you can always try writing me letters to win my favor.

If you notice any ink smudges or tears on the following pages, it's probably because of the sandstorm. So don't worry, the desert bandits know better than to mess with me.

I've traveled this trade route many times. It's always been so wild and unforgiving... yet also prosperous. Last time I was there, I still went by the name Madeleine.

Back then, all I wanted was to leave this wretched place with its terrible weather and worse temper, but it repaid my scorn with kindness by teaching me the best lesson in business I've ever learned.

It's another long story, and perhaps not a particularly interesting one. But I think you might be willing to hear it.
